flaws.title: Half-Cycle Frame Duplication (4 Poses Doubled into 8 Columns)
flaws.summary: Frames 5, 6, 7, and 8 are near-identical copies of Frames 1, 2, 3, and 4 rather than the second half of an 8-frame running stride.
flaws.quantitativeEvidence: Mean centroid-aligned silhouette IoU between Frame k and Frame k+4 is 94.7% (4 unique poses out of 8 columns per row; 24 unique poses out of 48 total cells).
flaws.biomechanicalImpact: Halves the effective animation resolution to 4 frames and causes the cycle to repeat twice per loop.
flaws.algorithmicFix: Evaluate continuous gait phase φ ∈ [0, 1) across 8 distinct 45° phase increments (φ = 0.000, 0.125, ..., 0.875) with zero duplicated poses.

flaws.title: Missing Alternating Gait — Unilateral "Peg-Leg" Hop
flaws.summary: Despite the sheet title claiming "(Alternating Gait)", the same leg (far leg) stays permanently extended in front and the near leg stays permanently behind across all 8 frames.
flaws.quantitativeEvidence: In all 8 frames, frontFootOffsetX > +45 px and rearFootOffsetX < -60 px with identical limb shading order; the left and right legs never swap lead.
flaws.biomechanicalImpact: A human runner alternates left and right lead legs every half-stride (180° phase offset) with opposite arm counter-rotation. Keeping one leg permanently ahead produces a comical one-legged limp/hop.
flaws.algorithmicFix: Drive the near (right) leg at phase φ and the far (left) leg at exact anti-phase (φ + 0.5) mod 1, with counter-phased arm swing and distinct near/far depth shading.

flaws.title: Zero Leg Crossover (Missing "Pass" / Recovery Phase)
flaws.summary: Neither leg ever passes beneath the pelvis; the legs remain permanently scissored apart in every frame.
flaws.quantitativeEvidence: Minimum horizontal foot-to-foot separation across all 8 frames is 147 px (a real run cycle crosses 0 px twice per stride during the Pass phase).
flaws.biomechanicalImpact: Without a passing pose where the swing knee overtakes the stance leg under the hip, the limbs appear to oscillate statically in place and snap backward instantly between Frame 4 and Frame 5/1.
flaws.algorithmicFix: Solve closed orbital foot trajectories where the stance foot sweeps backward on the ground via 2-bone IK while the swing knee drives forward past the hip at φ = 0.25 and φ = 0.75.

flaws.title: Unregistered Pivot & Counter-Physical Scale/Baseline Jitter
flaws.summary: Character body height, head volume, and ground contact line fluctuate erratically between adjacent cells.
flaws.quantitativeEvidence: Bounding-box height varies by 20 px (212 px to 232 px) and the raw cell ground baseline shifts by 25 px without matching ballistic flight phases.
flaws.biomechanicalImpact: Playing raw cell crops causes vertical popping and horizontal sliding, while the character shrinks during mid-stride.
flaws.algorithmicFix: Enforce invariant segment bone lengths (femur, tibia, trunk, humerus, forearm) from a single anatomical rig with double-frequency pelvis bob Δy(φ) locked to stance/flight physics.

flaws.title: Two-Tone Magenta Checkerboard & JPEG Chroma Spill
flaws.summary: The sheet combines #FF00FF grid lines over #FD49FD pink cell backgrounds with JPEG 8×8 block compression artifacts.
flaws.quantitativeEvidence: Cell backgrounds average RGB(253, 74, 253) while dividers are RGB(253, 0, 252), with 1–2 px magenta fringe bleed along dark outlines.
flaws.biomechanicalImpact: Naive single-color chroma keying leaves pink halos around the runner or accidentally erodes purple jersey pixels.
flaws.algorithmicFix: Use border-seeded flood-fill chroma keying with boundary despill for extraction, and render algorithmic sprites directly into clean RGBA buffers.
